Merced County Superior Court

The Merced County Superior Court serves as the primary judicial institution in Merced County, California. Located at 2260 N Street, Merced, CA 95340, this courthouse handles a wide range of legal matters, from traffic violations to complex civil litigation. Operating under the Court of Appeal Fifth District, the facility provides essential judicial services to Merced County residents.

Court Hours and Contact Information

  • Operating Hours: Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 3:00 PM
  • Phone: (209) 725-4111
  • Website: www.merced.courts.ca.gov
  • Weekend Hours: Closed Saturday and Sunday

Court Locations and Divisions

Merced County Superior Court operates through five main divisions:

Maintains confidential proceedings

Main Courthouse (N Street Building)

Address: 2260 N Street, Merced, CA 95340

Primary location for most court proceedings

Los Banos Division

Address: 1159 G Street, Los Banos, CA 93635

Serves the western portion of Merced County

Old Courthouse (21st Street Building)

Address: 627 W. 21st Street, Merced, CA 95340

Houses specific administrative offices

Traffic Division

Handles traffic violations and infractions

Processes citations from local law enforcement

Juvenile Division

Dedicated to juvenile court matters

Merced County Superior Court is a city courthouse in Merced County, California. It is located within. Court of appeal fifth district. The courthouse was established in 1855, but a permanent building was made in 1857; then, further advancement was made, and in 2007 the courthouse was combined into a single tilt-up concrete building. The court's mission is to assist the public trust and confidence in the judicial system by guaranteeing equal access to promote justice and serve the community with respect. It has jurisdiction over criminal, small claims, probation, juvenile, appeal, finance, civil, family, traffic, and vehicle matters. They provide services like online payment, forms, online case search, e-filing, court calendar and many more, so it is optional to go to court for these services. This court also provides self-help for a different division. Every person must follow local rules and wear a mask in this court. Proper dressing is required during the case hearing. Five superior courts located in this county are:

  • MERCED COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT – LOS BANOS DIVISION
  • MERCED COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT – NEW COURTHOUSE (N STREET BUILDING)
  • MERCED COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT – OLD COURTHOUSE (21ST STREET BUILDING)
  • MERCED COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT – TRAFFIC DIVISION
  • MERCED COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT – JUVENILE DIVISION

How to search for case information?

How to search for a case hearing?

Merced County Superior Court Case Search can be done online using the court portal https://jpportal.mercedcourt.org/mercedpublic. Registration on the portal for accessing case searches is not mandatory. The court maintains all the records online, in files or a database. The Search can be done in the following ways:

  • Search by Case Number, citation, record or traffic number
  • Search by First, middle and last name
  • Search by party name
  • Search by attorney name
  • Search by attorney bar number
  • Search by judicial officer
  • Search by courtroom

After entering the data, the case information will come. The portal will only show those records information that is publicly available. It does not show records of adoption, criminal, family, juvenile and mental health matters etc. Some records are unavailable; if the information does not come, the case records will be removed or confidential and cannot be displayed online. You have to go to the court or give a record request for these documents, and then the court will decide whether to provide that information. The fee for each document per page is $0.50, which is mandatory. All the guidelines related to different case searches and how to register on the portal search are available online on the website.

How To Find Merced Superior Court?

Merced Superior Court Is Located At 627 W. 21st Street, Merced, CA 95340. You Can Easily Find The Court By Using Google Maps Or Any Other Navigation App. The Court Is Open From Monday To Friday, From 8:00 A.M. To 5:00 P.M.

Services Provided By Merced Superior Court

Merced Superior Court Provides A Wide Range Of Services To The Public. These Services Include:

  • Filing And Processing Of Civil And Criminal Cases
  • Court Hearings And Trials
  • Jury Services
  • Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Services
  • Self-Help Services For People Representing Themselves In Court
  • Access To Court Records And Documents

Filing A Case In Merced Superior Court

If You Want To File A Case In Merced Superior Court, You Must First Determine The Appropriate Court To File Your Case In. Then, You Must Fill Out The Necessary Forms And Pay The Filing Fee. The Court Has Self-Help Centers That Provide Assistance To People Who Are Representing Themselves In Court.

Responding To A Case In Merced Superior Court

If You Have Been Served With A Lawsuit, You Must Respond To It Within A Certain Time Period. Failure To Respond Can Result In A Default Judgment Against You. You Can Respond To A Lawsuit By Filing An Answer Or A Motion To Dismiss.

Merced Superior Court Procedures

Merced Superior Court Has Procedures In Place To Ensure That Cases Are Handled Fairly And Efficiently. These Procedures Include:

  • Case Management Conferences
  • Discovery Procedures
  • Pre-Trial Conferences
  • Trial Procedures

Merced County Superior Court Court Fees

There Are Fees Associated With Filing A Case Or Requesting Services From Merced Superior Court. The Fees Vary Depending On The Type Of Case And The Service Requested. The Court Accepts Payment By Cash, Check, Or Credit Card.

Merced County Superior Court Records And Access

Court Records Are Public Records, Which Means That They Can Be Accessed By Anyone. Merced Superior Court Provides Various Ways To Access Court Records, Including:

  • Online Access Through The Court’s Website
  • In-Person Access At The Courthouse
  • Requesting Records By Mail

How can I make a payment in merced county court?

Merced Traffic Court payment can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

A person can pay for tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the court payment office. Take your ticket, citation number, courtesy notice or any other information representing your cases when you are coming for payment. 2.5% surcharges will be applied if you make payment with a credit card. The schedule for a walk-in payment can be changed, so contact the court before you come for payment.

Online

Merced court's online payments can be made using the Superior Court Online Portal https://jpportal.mercedcourt.org/MERCEDPUBLIC/Home/Dashboard/17. Enter any search type like a case number, name etc. and enter criteria. Your case information with the amount of the fine will be displayed. Select the payment option and pay the amount online.

Mail

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address; 720 West 20th Street, Merced, CA 95340 or to the Merced Court's Los Banos Division at 1159 G Street, Los Banos, CA 93635. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted. Remember to write your citation, name, case number and account number when you send the payment, and mail the amount in a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you want a receipt.

Drop Box

One can also pay in an envelope and put it in the court's front door drop box. Write your name, address and citation number on the envelope.

How can I appear remotely?

Merced County Superior Court's remote appearance can be done using the zoom application or by telephone. Fill out the virtual hearing form and send it to the court; the court will give you a schedule with a meeting link if your case is eligible for a virtual hearing. Join the session 10 minutes before the schedule. Make sure your internet connection is strong. Mute your microphone and speak only when the judge calls your name. Rules, forms and procedures for each case division are available remotely. Please read them before your schedule.

Merced Court Family law handles which type of cases?

Merced Court Family law matters are handled by the New Merced Courthouse N Building and deal with all types of issues related to the family. The issues include:

  • Divorce, legal separation or nullity of marriage
  • Child custody and visitation issues
  • Child, Spousal and Family support issues
  • Domestic Violence
  • Elder abuse issue
  • Adoption issues

They also provide family court services for the Recommending Counseling of Child Custody. Giving legal advice is not allowed; you must hire a private attorney for any advice related to the case.

The traffic division handles which type of cases?

Merced County Court Traffic Division handles cases related to traffic, vehicle and speeding ticket violations. The violation includes speeding, accident, violation of vehicle code, infraction, minor felony cases, local municipal ordinance, violation of traffic signal, driving without a license, and suspended license. This division is also responsible for the citation filing from different law enforcement agencies in this county. If you received a traffic ticket or citation, and mandatory appearance is written on it, then you must appear on your schedule; otherwise, pay the fine, enter a plea or sign up for the traffic school. If you need help, contact the traffic divisions by visiting or calling during regular hours.

The probate court handles which type of cases?

Merced County Court probate court handles the probation cases that include estates of the decedent, trusts, minors’ guardianship, and adults' and minors' compromise conservatorships. They had a probate examiner responsible for reviewing the probate proceedings filings and ensuring that all files complied with the probate code and state and local rules.

Alternative Dispute Resolution

Merced Superior Court Offers Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Services As An Alternative To Traditional Court Proceedings. ADR Can Be Less Expensive And Less Time-Consuming Than Going To Trial. The Court Provides Several ADR Options, Including Mediation And Arbitration.

Jury Duty In Merced Superior Court

Jury Duty Is An Important Part Of The Judicial System, And Merced Superior Court Relies On The Participation Of Jurors To Ensure A Fair Trial. If You Are Summoned For Jury Duty, You Must Report To The Courthouse At The Specified Time And Date. The Court Will Compensate You For Your Time And Expenses.

Merced Superior Court Judges

Merced Superior Court Has Several Judges Who Preside Over Cases. The Judges Are Responsible For Ensuring That Cases Are Handled Fairly And Efficiently. They Also Make Decisions Based On The Law And The Evidence Presented In Court.

Appeals From Merced Superior Court

If You Are Unhappy With The Outcome Of Your Case In Merced Superior Court, You May Be Able To Appeal The Decision. Appeals Are Heard By The California Court Of Appeal, Which Is Located In Fresno, California.

Tips For Representing Yourself In Merced Superior Court

Representing Yourself In Court Can Be Challenging, But It Is Possible. Merced Superior Court Provides Self-Help Services For People Who Cannot Afford An Attorney. Some Tips For Representing Yourself In Court Include:

  • Researching The Law And Court Procedures
  • Being Prepared And Organized
  • Dressing Appropriately For Court
  • Being Respectful To The Judge And Other Court Personnel
  • Being Honest And Truthful

Hiring An Attorney For Merced Superior Court

If You Can Afford An Attorney, It Is Highly Recommended That You Hire One. An Attorney Can Provide Legal Advice And Guidance, As Well As Represent You In Court. You Can Find An Attorney Through A Referral From A Friend Or Family Member, Or By Contacting The Merced County Bar Association.

Merced Superior Court Case Search

Merced Superior Court Offers An Online Case Search Tool That Allows You To Search For Cases By Case Number, Party Name, Or Filing Date. This Is A Convenient Way To Access Information About Your Case Or To Search For Information About Other Cases In The Court System.

Merced Superior Court Phone Number

The Phone Number For Merced Superior Court Is (209) 725-4111. You Can Call This Number To Reach The Court’s Main Office And Speak To A Court Clerk Or Get Information About Court Services.

Merced Superior Court Address

The Address For Merced Superior Court Is 627 W. 21st Street, Merced, CA 95340. This Is The Location Of The Court’s Main Office And Courthouse.

Merced Superior Court Live Stream

Merced Superior Court Does Not Currently Offer A Live Stream Of Court Proceedings. However, The Court Does Provide Access To Court Records And Offers Video Conferencing For Some Court Proceedings.

Merced County Superior Court Civil Case Search

Merced County Superior Court Offers An Online Civil Case Search Tool That Allows You To Search For Civil Cases By Case Number Or Party Name. This Tool Provides Access To Information About Civil Cases In The Court System.

Merced County Court Clerk’s Office

The Merced County Court Clerk’s Office Is Responsible For Maintaining Court Records And Providing Access To Court Documents. The Office Is Located At 627 W. 21st Street, Merced, CA 95340, And Can Be Reached By Phone At (209) 725-4111.
